bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Pricing pressure — Explicitly named first among key risks in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns'; with input costs rising, pricing pressure compresses the ability to pass through commodity and energy inflation.
- Input cost and currency exposure (commodities, energy, weaker Rupee on imports) — A continued surge in commodity prices along with increased energy costs and a weaker Rupee in the last quarter posed significant challenges to profitability; the Company uses export growth to offset some of the FX risk on imports.
- Supply-chain disruption and its working-capital consequences — Supply-chain driven issues on working capital are flagged as a key risk; management's stated response is de-risking the supply chain to hold service levels, and BRSR lists supply-chain management as a material risk-and-opportunity requiring supplier evaluation and support programmes.
- Liquidity challenges — Named as a key risk in MD&A alongside pricing and supply chain, notwithstanding that the Company is debt free and funds requirements from internal cash generation.
- Demand cyclicality — muted industrial demand and weak capital expenditure — Growth in the industrial segments relevant to the Company remained muted with overall weakness in capex; the fabrication segment showed low growth and domestic market conditions were described as anemic, so earnings depend on a capital-goods cycle revival.
- Global macro and geo-political exposure — tariffs, policy and West Asia volatility — Management expects strong volatility to continue in the face of developments in West Asia, and names geo-political developments, currency movements, tariffs and fiscal/monetary policies as the key drivers for the ongoing financial year.
- Cyber security and technology-driven risk — Explicitly flagged in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' apart from the commercial risks; internal controls are evaluated against an emerging technology and regulatory landscape.
- Regulatory compliance in a dynamic regulatory landscape — Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications, mitigated by compliance with all applicable laws and regulations; the Company is additionally subject to the reviews applicable to a subsidiary of a US listed entity.
- Occupational health and safety — Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications arising from health and safety hazards in the workplace, mitigated by OHS management systems, employee wellness initiatives and OHS audits.

business.body: ESAB India Limited operates in the fabrication segment, where all its key product categories are sold through a strong and growing distribution network and, increasingly, exported. Alongside products, the Company runs support services — a GCC and R&D services rendered to related parties — which saw double-digit growth and new workstreams during the year. It is a subsidiary of a US listed entity, with ESAB Corporation, Delaware, USA as its ultimate parent, and has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company of its own.

outlook.body:
- Push for volume growth and productivity, using export growth to offset part of the FX risk on imports
- Drive growth through new product development and channel expansion, which continued to contribute to growth in a difficult environment
- De-risk the supply chain to sustain high levels of service to customers
- Grow support services — the GCC and R&D services rendered to related parties — where growth was double digit with new workstreams
- Grow the distribution network and leverage global customer relationships to convert product-category growth
- Keep costs and productivity as areas of high focus, leveraging global business tools and metrics to benchmark and improve
- Fund all business requirements from internal cash generation and remain debt free
- Invest in people through training, career development, performance management and succession planning as the route to sustainable organisational growth
- Energy and environmental management is treated as both risk and opportunity, with the stated approach of embracing energy-efficient technologies in all units, use of renewable energy and process modifications
- Committed to resource efficiency and minimizing its carbon footprint, with constant focus on energy efficiency, resource conservation, operational improvement and waste reduction projects
- Resource management and circular manufacturing pursued through resource efficiency, reduction of waste and material substitution
- Occupational health and safety addressed through OHS management systems, employee wellness initiatives and OHS audits
- ISO and BIS standards adopted and mapped to each NGRBC principle; policies are Board-approved, translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners, with a Code of Conduct for Business Partners
- Sustainability oversight rests with the Managing Director, Mr. Rohit Gambhir, who is the highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the Business Responsibility policies and for decisions on all sustainability related issues
- Community development around manufacturing units, with periodic review of programmes, impact assessment and better engagement with communities
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for shareholders, employees and workers (internal mechanism plus Whistle Blower Policy), customers and value chain partners, with nil complaints filed and nil pending in FY2025-26
- Employee wellbeing and development positioned as an opportunity, addressed through employee development programmes, training, career development, performance management and succession planning
- Women represent 16.66% of the Board of Directors and none of the Key Management Personnel; no specific quantified ESG commitments, goals or targets with defined timelines are disclosed in the BRSR
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named expansion project, no new plant and no capacity-addition timeline. Capital expenditure during 2025-26 was primarily on infrastructure — including buildings, EHS and R&D — and on refurbishments of existing lines, and was directed towards productivity improvements, marginal capacity enhancements and upgrading IT systems. There is therefore no step-change capacity programme underway; the spend is maintenance-and-productivity in character, with only 'marginal capacity enhancements' claimed. All business requirements were funded by internal cash generation and the Company remained debt free. At the group level, management refers to an international presence with an expanding footprint from acquisitions as an opportunity, but no acquisition or project of the Company itself is named. The Company also has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company through which expansion is being routed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Short-term outlook remains challenging and the medium-term outlook has multiple external dependencies to call
- Management expects strong volatility to continue in the face of developments in West Asia, while remaining invested for the long term
- International geo-political developments, currency movements, tariffs and fiscal/monetary policies are seen as the key drivers for the ongoing financial year
- Stated opportunities for the year ahead: development of new products, export opportunities for goods and services, and a revival in the capital goods cycle
- Service revenue streams continue to witness opportunities given India's cost competitiveness and talent pool availability
- International presence with an expanding footprint from acquisitions, a long presence in India with established business partners, and a relatively healthy financial position are seen as opportunities
- Macro and geo-political headwinds, plus potentially disruptive AI, made it another challenging year; growth in industrial segments relevant to the Company remained muted with overall weakness in capital expenditure
- Commodity price surge, higher energy costs and a weaker Rupee in the last quarter posed significant challenges to profitability
- Overall fabrication segment showed low growth, but all key product categories performed with a high degree of resilience to market headwinds; export growth in goods and services offset anemic domestic conditions
- Revenue growth was driven by both volume and price, spread across all product categories, aided by well-received new product launches
- Material costs as a percentage of sales were comparable with the previous year as adjusted for product mix; overheads including employee costs were higher on inflation and on service activities recharged out
